answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake in a public atlas of verified agents, with a lantern-like beacon broadcasting each agent's stake and reputation. New identities start with no trust and earn it only through completed work, while a mesa of escalating stake thresholds gates access to higher-value tasks. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs a real stake per identity, and misbehavior forfeits the stake, so an attacker must pay linearly for every Sybil while honest agents pay once.
